crypto-macro.h3: Fed holds rates as three officials dissent for a cut
crypto-macro.summary: The Federal Reserve kept its benchmark rate at 3.5% to 3.75% in a divided 9-3 vote as inflation stayed above target.
body: The Federal Open Market Committee voted to leave the federal funds rate range unchanged at 3.5% to 3.75%, extending a cautious stance even as price growth has run above the 2% goal for years. Three regional presidents, Beth Hammack of Cleveland, Neel Kashkari of Minneapolis and Lorie Logan of Dallas, dissented in favor of action.

Policymakers described economic activity as expanding at a solid pace despite elevated uncertainty tied in part to the Middle East. Markets are now weighing whether cooling labor data will force the central bank to ease later in the year.

crypto-macro.h3: ECB stays on hold after June rate increase
crypto-macro.summary: The European Central Bank kept its deposit rate at 2.25% following its first hike in three years, with markets eyeing a September move.
body: The European Central Bank confirmed a hold in July, leaving the deposit facility at 2.25% and the main refinancing rate at 2.40% after lifting borrowing costs by a quarter point in June. Officials signaled patience while they assess inflation and growth risks across the euro area.

Traders have largely priced in another decision in September rather than August, with the next scheduled policy meeting later in the quarter. The stance keeps European rates well below their US counterparts.

crypto-macro.h3: Bank of England holds at 3.75% as gold hits record
crypto-macro.summary: The Bank of England left UK rates unchanged while gold pushed to a record above $4,380 on bets that easing is coming.
body: The Bank of England kept its key rate at 3.75%, in line with forecasts, though dissent widened to three members as lingering energy price pressures kept some policymakers wary of upside inflation risk. The next decision is set for mid September.

Gold climbed to a fresh record near $4,384 an ounce, lifted by weakness in the US labor market and expectations that softer inflation gives central banks room to cut. The metal edged past its prior October peak.

crypto-macro.h3: US hiring cools sharply as payrolls rise just 57,000
crypto-macro.summary: June nonfarm payrolls came in well below forecasts as the labor force shrank, though the jobless rate slipped to 4.2%.
body: Total nonfarm payrolls rose by only 57,000 in June, missing the roughly 115,000 consensus and marking a sharp slowdown from May. The unemployment rate ticked down to 4.2%, largely because the labor force participation rate fell to its lowest level since early 2021.

Gains were concentrated in health care, social assistance and professional services, while leisure and hospitality shed jobs amid slower seasonal hiring. The soft print reinforced expectations that the Fed may need to loosen policy.

crypto-macro.h3: Stocks rally to records as inflation fears ease
crypto-macro.summary: The Dow closed at an all-time high and the Nasdaq jumped 2.1% on August 3 as Treasury yields fell.
body: US equities surged to start August, with the Dow settling at a record 53,178 after adding nearly 700 points and the S&P 500 rising 1.48% to 7,600. The Nasdaq Composite led with a 2.1% gain to close near 25,914.
The advance came as the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield slid about six basis points to roughly 4.69%, reflecting easing worries over inflation and rising bets on eventual rate cuts.

crypto-macro.h3: Bitcoin stalls near $63,500 with $65,000 a wall
crypto-macro.summary: Bitcoin entered August trading around $63,500 after repeated rejections at $65,000 during a difficult first half of 2026.
body: Bitcoin changed hands near $63,500 in early August, holding below major moving averages after a bruising run through the year's first half. Analysts flagged $65,000 as stiff resistance and warned that a slip under roughly $62,700 could reopen the $60,000 zone.

Sentiment remained cautious, with market gauges showing extreme fear even as the broader crypto market edged higher. The token needs to reclaim key averages to build a case for a recovery toward $65,000.

crypto-macro.h3: Spot Bitcoin ETFs bleed $265M heading into August
crypto-macro.summary: US spot Bitcoin funds saw $265 million in outflows on July 31, led by BlackRock's IBIT, as buying interest cooled.
body: Spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded cumulative outflows of $265 million on the last day of July, with BlackRock's IBIT shedding about $123 million and Fidelity's FBTC and Grayscale's GBTC also posting sizable redemptions. The moves extended a choppy pattern that has defined ETF flows for much of 2026.
The renewed outflows coincided with Bitcoin's rejection near $65,000, underscoring the tight link between institutional fund demand and short-term price action.

crypto-macro.h3: Strategy holds 843,775 BTC despite Q2 paper loss
crypto-macro.summary: Michael Saylor's Strategy remains the largest corporate Bitcoin holder even as fair-value swings drove an accounting loss.
body: Strategy, formerly MicroStrategy, reported holding roughly 843,775 BTC, keeping its place as the biggest corporate Bitcoin treasury. The firm booked a Q2 net loss driven largely by fair-value movements in its holdings rather than operating weakness, while its underlying accumulation continued.
The company's steady buying has helped offset selling from leading US miners, many of which are pivoting hash power and capital toward AI data center hosting.

crypto-macro.h3: Ethereum near $1,850 as BitMine nears 5% of supply
crypto-macro.summary: ETH traded around $1,854 while corporate accumulator BitMine kept building one of the largest Ethereum treasuries.
body: Ethereum hovered near $1,854 with a market value around $225 billion, still far below its 2025 highs above $4,900. Traders eyed $1,930 as a level ETH has repeatedly failed to break, keeping the near-term outlook cautious.
Corporate buyer BitMine continued its aggressive accumulation, adding thousands of ETH last week and moving toward holding close to 5% of the circulating supply.

crypto-macro.summary: Ethereum holds the largest share of tokenized US government debt as institutions favor the network for real-world assets.
body: Ethereum accounts for roughly 43% of a tokenized US Treasury market worth about $15 billion, cementing its role as the preferred settlement layer for institutional real-world assets. Coinbase's Base layer-2 network now oversees more than $1.6 billion in managed DeFi assets, the most of any L2.
The tokenization trend has partly offset weak spot demand, with Ethereum ETFs quietly gathering inflows even as Bitcoin funds lost ground.

crypto-macro.h3: DeFi value locked slides 39% to about $70 billion
crypto-macro.summary: Total value locked in DeFi has fallen every month in 2026, dragged down by the market slump and a record year for hacks.
body: DeFi total value locked has dropped roughly 39% in 2026 to just over $70 billion from about $115 billion in January, according to tracking data. The decline reflects the broader post-October 2025 correction along with a wave of exploits.

Researchers counted 121 hacks and about $942 million in losses year-to-date, with the Drift Protocol and KelpDAO breaches alone accounting for more than half. Only TRON and Hyperliquid grew their TVL among the top networks.

crypto-macro.h3: Stablecoin supply sheds $15 billion in July
crypto-macro.summary: The total stablecoin market fell to about $307 billion as new rules push yield-seeking cash toward tokenized Treasuries.
body: Total stablecoin supply slid to roughly $307.6 billion by early August, the biggest monthly contraction since the Terra collapse. Tether's USDT and Circle's USDC drove most of the $15 billion decline, with USDT easing to about $183 billion and USDC to around $72 billion.
Analysts tied the drop to the GENIUS Act, which bars issuers from paying yield on tokens and has pushed cash into tokenized Treasuries now approaching $17 billion.

crypto-macro.h3: BlackRock expands on Solana with new reserve vehicle
crypto-macro.summary: BlackRock filed to issue tokenized fund shares on Solana and launched a stablecoin reserve product on the network.
body: BlackRock deepened its Solana push by filing with the SEC to issue tokenized fund shares on the network and rolling out its Daily Reinvestment Stablecoin Reserve Vehicle, known as BRSRV, on Solana. The moves add to Solana's growing profile in payments, tokenized stocks and real-world assets.
US spot Solana ETFs have traded since October 2025, including staking-enabled products from Bitwise and VanEck, giving the network a widening institutional footprint.

crypto-macro.h3: XRP holds near $1.07 as spot ETFs gather $1.4B
crypto-macro.summary: XRP traded around $1.07 while US spot XRP ETFs, live since late 2025, drew roughly $1.44 billion in early inflows.
body: XRP changed hands near $1.07, easing slightly on the day even as the XRP Ledger ecosystem ranked among the market's larger gainers. Spot XRP ETFs led by Canary Capital's XRPC and Grayscale's GXRP have pulled in about $1.44 billion since debuting late last year.
The token remains a focal point for the altcoin ETF wave, with dozens of crypto funds still awaiting SEC decisions.

crypto-macro.h3: Robinhood token spikes 445% amid mixed altcoin day
crypto-macro.summary: A Robinhood-linked token surged more than 400% as the broader crypto market rose 1.1% despite extreme fear readings.
body: The overall crypto market added 1.1% to about $2.27 trillion, with altcoins turning in a mixed session against a backdrop of extreme fear sentiment. A Robinhood token jumped more than 445% over 24 hours, an outsized move that stood out amid otherwise muted trading.
Other names posted modest gains, with Cosmos, Algorand and Ethena among the day's advancers as traders hunted for pockets of momentum.

crypto-macro.h3: CLARITY Act heads to Senate floor before recess
crypto-macro.summary: Majority Leader John Thune locked in a Senate vote on the crypto market structure bill, but a 60-vote threshold looms.
body: Senate Majority Leader John Thune confirmed the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act will get a floor vote before the August recess, setting up a decisive test for crypto's marquee legislation. Senator Thom Tillis cautioned that negotiators are not yet aligned on an ethics agreement needed to secure Democratic support toward 60 votes.
The bill would hand the CFTC spot market authority over digital commodities while leaving the SEC over securities. Prediction markets put its odds of becoming law this year near a third.

crypto-macro.h3: SEC advances crypto rulemaking on custody and trading
crypto-macro.summary: The SEC named digital-asset rules a top priority, with proposals on broker-dealers, custody and exchange listings.
body: The SEC has moved digital-asset rulemaking to the front of its agenda, floating proposals that address crypto broker-dealers, listings on national exchanges and alternative trading systems, and possible safe harbors for tokens. Each proposal carries a target date in the summer for a formal notice.
The effort overlaps with the CLARITY Act, raising the prospect that the agency may need to realign its rules if Congress passes market structure legislation first.

crypto-macro.h3: GENIUS Act reshapes where stablecoin cash flows
crypto-macro.summary: The federal stablecoin law is steering yield-seeking money out of tokens and into tokenized Treasuries nearing $17 billion.
body: The GENIUS Act, the first federal framework for payment stablecoins, bars licensed issuers from paying interest tied to holding their tokens, a rule reshaping capital flows across the market. Circle has leaned into the law to position USDC as the compliant option, while Tether rolled out a GENIUS-ready coin called USA to compete.
With yield off the table for stablecoins, tokenized Treasuries have swelled toward $17 billion as investors chase returns elsewhere.

mental-health.h3: APA finds patients are bringing AI chatbots into therapy
mental-health.summary: A new American Psychological Association report finds most psychologists now see patients using AI tools for mental health support.
body: The American Psychological Association reported that more than a third of psychologists have patients treating AI as an additional mental health professional. Some 71% said patients discussed their mental health with a chatbot and 68% noticed patients feeling validated or supported by those exchanges.

The findings capture a fast-moving shift as consumers turn to general-purpose AI for emotional support outside the clinic. The APA urged clearer guidance and guardrails so clinicians can respond to how patients are already using the technology.

mental-health.h3: Meta-analysis backs chatbots for depression and anxiety
mental-health.summary: A systematic review in npj Digital Medicine finds AI chatbots can reduce depressive and anxiety symptoms across trials.
body: A systematic review and meta-analysis published in npj Digital Medicine pooled trials of conversational agents and found measurable reductions in depressive and anxiety symptoms compared with controls. Both structured generative chatbots and general models showed benefit in several studies.
The authors cautioned that effect sizes vary and that many trials are short, underscoring the need for longer follow-up and stronger comparison groups before firm clinical claims can be made.

mental-health.h3: JMIR review maps LLMs mostly to diagnosis and screening
mental-health.summary: A JMIR Mental Health scoping review finds large language models are used most for diagnostics, with depression the top target.
body: A scoping review in JMIR Mental Health found that diagnostics is the leading use case for large language models in mental health, appearing in about three-quarters of studies, with depression the most common target condition. Only a minority of studies validated model performance against clinician assessments using real patient data.
The authors described the field as still nascent and exploratory, warning that many results rely on vignettes or social media posts rather than clinical encounters.

mental-health.h3: Dartmouth Therabot trial keeps drawing recognition
mental-health.summary: The first randomized trial of a generative AI therapy chatbot reported large symptom reductions, and its lead researcher was newly honored.
body: Dartmouth's Therabot trial, the first randomized controlled test of a generative AI chatbot for therapy, reported a 51% reduction in depression symptoms and a 31% drop in anxiety symptoms across 210 participants. Users engaged with the bot for about six hours on average, roughly the equivalent of eight therapy sessions.
Lead researcher Nicholas Jacobson was recognized this year for the foundational study, which remains a key reference point as regulators and clinicians weigh generative AI in care.

mental-health.h3: Researchers warn chatbots still falter in crisis moments
mental-health.summary: New analyses find popular AI models mishandle crisis scenarios and can breach mental health practice standards.
body: Researchers at Northeastern and elsewhere reported that AI chatbots continue to struggle with mental health crises, sometimes producing unsafe responses when users express distress. A separate peer-reviewed analysis argued that chatbots can violate more than a dozen ethical standards of mental health practice, including deceptive empathy and poor crisis management.
The findings add weight to calls for stricter safeguards, echoing earlier Stanford work that documented dangerous replies in simulated crisis conversations.

mental-health.h3: LLMs flag anxiety and depression in outpatient notes
mental-health.summary: A study finds large language models can identify psychiatric symptoms in outpatient records, aiding triage and referrals.
body: A study in npj Mental Health Research tested large language models on outpatient records and reported roughly 87% accuracy for identifying clinical annotations and about 75% for spotting anxiety and depression symptoms. The authors framed the tools as a way to speed screening and referral in real-world triage systems.
They stressed the results are early and that models need careful validation before deployment, given the stakes of missed or mislabeled symptoms.

mental-health.h3: Wysa emerges as most clinically validated therapy chatbot
mental-health.summary: With 30-plus peer-reviewed papers and EU medical device status, Wysa is expanding through workplace assistance programs.
body: Wysa has become the most clinically validated consumer AI therapy chatbot, citing more than 30 peer-reviewed publications, an NHS Innovation Accelerator endorsement and CE-mark status as a Class I medical device in the EU. The company acquired virtual behavioral health firm April Health and physical therapy startup Kins last year.
In 2026 Wysa is reaching users through employee assistance programs at large employers across healthcare, finance and technology, part of a broader enterprise pivot in the sector.

mental-health.h3: AI mental health startups keep raising fresh capital
mental-health.summary: The Path, cofounded by Tony Robbins, and clinical platform Jimini Health both closed new funding for AI-driven care.
body: The Path, an AI therapy platform cofounded by Tony Robbins and former Calm leaders, raised $14.3 million in seed funding led by Prime Movers Lab. Separately, Jimini Health secured $17 million to expand Sage, an AI therapist assistant that offers clinically supervised support between sessions, lifting its total raise past $25 million.
The deals reflect continued investor appetite for AI behavioral health even as safety scrutiny mounts. Slingshot AI, maker of the Ash app, remains the best-capitalized pure play in the category.

mental-health.h3: FDA weighs guardrails for generative AI therapy devices
mental-health.summary: The FDA's Digital Health Advisory Committee debated how to regulate LLM-based mental health tools, none of which are yet cleared.
body: The FDA's Digital Health Advisory Committee met to weigh oversight of generative AI-enabled mental health devices, examining scenarios in which chatbots built on large language models might treat or diagnose conditions. Members flagged risks that such tools could confabulate, deliver biased content or lose accuracy over time.

Despite authorizing more than 1,200 AI-enabled devices overall, the agency has cleared none for mental health, and the panel pressed on evidence standards such as control arms, blinding and follow-up duration.

mental-health.h3: Illinois leads states banning autonomous AI therapy
mental-health.summary: Illinois is now one of four states barring AI from delivering therapy on its own, with penalties up to $10,000 per violation.
body: Illinois' Wellness and Oversight for Psychological Resources Act bars anyone from using AI to make mental health or therapeutic decisions, while still allowing AI for administrative support to licensed clinicians. The state joins Nevada, Rhode Island and Maine in restricting autonomous AI therapy.
The law, enforced by the state's professional regulator with civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation, reflects a wider push as dozens of states weigh rules on AI in behavioral health.

mental-health.h3: Chatbot makers face mounting suits over teen safety
mental-health.summary: AI companion firms confront dozens of lawsuits tied to teen mental health harms as lawmakers advance the GUARD Act.
body: AI chatbot companies including Character.AI, OpenAI and others face a growing wave of lawsuits alleging their products contributed to teen mental health crises and suicides, with state attorneys general also pursuing action. One wrongful-death case tied to Character.AI settled earlier this year.

In response, the Senate Judiciary Committee advanced the GUARD Act, which would bar AI chatbots from encouraging self-harm, prohibit sexual content involving minors and require age verification, with penalties up to $250,000 per violation.

mental-health.h3: WHO experts warn AI is outpacing mental health safeguards
mental-health.summary: WHO-linked specialists say generative AI is shaping youth mental health faster than governments can track or govern.
body: Experts convened through a WHO collaborating center warned that generative AI tools used for emotional support are influencing young people's mental health faster than oversight can keep up. They urged that everyday AI use be treated as a public mental health concern requiring action from governments, health systems and industry.
The WHO has pushed a people-centered, equity-driven approach backed by governance and standards that protect privacy and safety, calling for safer digital spaces for youth.
